craft_notes: Sthāyin: Courage of refuge (utsāha). Semicolon→comma (finding softens onto owning). Rejected: 'kens' for 'wots' — wots is older; kept. Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: E'en Brahmā finds his Brahmā in thee, whose master
owns thee no master, Master of masters? World's weal on weal — how vast thou? Who wots?
l4.sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇo 'pi bhavān brahma kasya neśas tvam īśituḥ jagatkalyāṇakalyāṇaṃ kiyat tvam iti vetti kaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Even of Brahmā you are Brahmā; of whom are you not lord, O lord of lords. → Lord of lords beyond measure — who knows how great?
c1_essence: Brahmā in you; unlorded by none; measure past measure.

l2.plain_english: Brahmā himself has Brahmā in you; what master owns no master in you, master of masters? Bliss of the world's bliss — who gauges how huge you are?
l2.sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇo 'pi bhavān brahma kasya neśas tvam īśituḥ jagatkalyāṇakalyāṇaṃ kiyat tvam iti vetti kaḥ
